items.title: 68514_Horace Henderson oral history interview
items.q: we had a guy on trombone, as I told you, Big Green from Nebraska.

ctx.x: The great Spoon, as we called him. And so they began to sing the blues. 'Ain't Nobody's Business' -- Lady Day had blues things. Not only, cause she had everything, you know, but these particular guys sang the blues, and the boss of the club would book these guys in, so we began to lean toward these blues patterns. (unintelligible). But you know who could play the blues in the band? Coleman Hawkins. Yes sir. He could play some of the filthiest -- and you had to like it, you know. And the

guys would -- we had trumpet players and all that, but Hawk would -- he'd growl, you know, and you begin to think in that vein. And the blues singers loved the thing. So you just begin to think blues, and we had a guy on trombone, as I told you, Big Green from Nebraska. He could play the blues. Och. So it rubs off on you, you know. After you hear the guys, you'd walk down the street and little riffs (unintelligible) begin to come to you. I love blues.
But you really hand't played blues much prior to that time.
